title: The 5 Most Powerful Rockets Ever Launched, Ranked (Apollo's Is Only #5)

scenes.text: The Apollo Moon rocket only makes number five. Number one pushes twice as hard.

scenes.label: Saturn V · 7.5M lbf
scenes.text: Number five: Saturn V. About seven and a half million pounds of thrust, enough to send people to the Moon.

scenes.label: Energia · 7.9M lbf
scenes.text: Number four: Energia, the Soviet launcher built to carry the Buran shuttle. About seven point nine million pounds.

scenes.label: SLS · 8.8M lbf
scenes.text: Number three: NASA's SLS. About eight point eight million pounds, and it launched Artemis one in twenty twenty-two.

scenes.label: N1 · 10M lbf
scenes.text: Number two: the Soviet N1. Over ten million pounds from thirty engines, but all four launches failed.

scenes.label: Starship · 16M+ lbf
scenes.text: Number one: SpaceX Starship. More than sixteen million pounds from thirty-three engines. Nothing has pushed harder.

description:
The five most powerful rockets ever launched, ranked by liftoff thrust.
The rocket that put people on the Moon is only number five, and number one has more than twice its thrust.
Which rocket would you have wanted to watch launch?
first_comment: Would you ride Starship or SLS? And what should we rank next?
